attempted_claim: Work in a saturated differentially closed field of characteristic zero U with derivation delta and constant field C. Let m>=3 and n>=3 and let f,g in Q[c][x] be polynomials of degrees m,n with coefficient tuples c algebraically independent over Q. Let X_{f,g}={x in U: delta^2 x+f(x)delta x+g(x)=0}. Prove or disprove that X_{f,g} is strongly minimal and geometrically trivial, i.e. orthogonal in U to C and to the Manin kernel of every simple abelian variety over acl(c,t) not descending to C. A complete answer is a rigorous proof that X_{f,g} has Morley rank 1, plus either (a) a forking-calculus witness of geometric triviality (independence of any two distinct nonalgebraic solutions and no nonconstant definable finite-to-finite correspondence from X_{f,g} to C or to any such Manin kernel), or (b) an explicit definable witness of non-orthogonality to C or to a named Manin kernel.
claim_type: strong minimality plus geometric triviality decision
decisive_failure: Strong minimality and geometric triviality of generic Lienard X_{f,g} remain unproved: the r>=2 Puiseux exclusion, the general resonant r=1 fiber closure, and the trichotomy lift to constants and Manin kernels are all missing and cannot be added in this expired-budget pass.
